questions.stem: A surgeon attended a wedding party and had a few drinks. After the marriage party he performed a surgery. His colleagues noticed that his hands were visibly shaking while he was operating, couldn’t maintain balance while standing and he was slurring while speaking. During surgery, a major blood vessel was ruptured leading to death. Which of these would be applicable for the surgeon?
questions.solutionHtml:
Criminal Negligence
  • Criminal negligence is when a person does an act which is in regard to the obvious risk to the safety of human life.
  • In this case, the surgeon was well aware of his drunk condition even before starting the surgery and was visibly affected due to this. Neglecting the obvious after effects of drinking and carrying on with the surgery which led to the blood vessel rupture and eventually, death makes the surgeon directly responsible for the patient’s death.
  • Criminal Negligence is statutorily embodied in section 304A of Indian Penal Code (IPC) – Causing Death by negligence: “Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years. Or with fine, or with both”.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 40.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the firearm injury shown in the image below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pistol, Near Range

Here the image shows primary bullet injury along with tattooing effect due to gunpowder; and absence of large central stellate wound (s/o close shot) or pellet injuries which is suggestive of Pistol injury, near range



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 221,222,228.

questions.stem: A 40 yr old male with alopecia came to the hospital. His wife complains of some behavioral abnormalities in him. Physical examination revealed loss of eyebrows and eyelashes on the lateral part. Doctor notices some abnormal findings on the patient's nails. Which of the following can be the type of poisoning in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thallium

Patient with alopecia, Loss of eyebrow , abnormal (dystrophy ?) nails.and behavioral abnormality point towards diagnosis of Thallium poisoning.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number-- 548

questions.stem: During a certain trial, the lawyer of the defendant asked a leading question and the opposite lawyer quickly raised an objection. The judge sustained the appeal and requested the defense lawyer to avoid asking such questions. Leading questions can't be allowed in any of the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cross Examination

Leading questions can only be asked during cross-examination and not during examination-in-chief or re-examination unless and until the court allows.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 14

questions.stemHtml: Identify the wound in the image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Defence Wounds

The image showed a wound on the palmar side of hand ,suggesting he/she was trying to grasp the weapon; the wound is also noted along fingers suggesting some double edged weapon is likely the crime weapon.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 207
